headline: 英國新書談創傷與戒酒
context: 新書《Sky City》，作者賈桂琳．克魯克斯（Jacqueline Crooks），描寫一名在1990年代倫敦公宅長大的女性潔西（Jaycee）。她童年遭繼父性侵，母親卻視而不見，後來被安置到寄養機構，與另一名同樣受創的女孩艾拉-G，建立起深厚的友誼。同一天，主持人約翰．羅賓斯（John Robins）推出有聲回憶錄《Thirst》，講述他從七歲偷喝酒，到後來走向戒酒的歷程。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A young woman is haunted by her childhood in this forcefully imaginative and unapologetically bleak novel from the author of Fire Rush The world of Sky City never quite settles beneath your feet. The action of Jacqueline Crooks’s second novel unfolds in a recognisable 1990s London, yet everything seems subtly untethered from reality: a council estate suspended above the city, voices drifting in and out through pirate radio, ghosts walking beside the living. The narrative floats just above the surface of the everyday, a world where trauma transforms the mundane into something uncanny. We first meet protagonist Jaycee as a child, trapped in a west London housing estate she calls the Cyborg House. Her stepfather subjects her to horrific sexual abuse while her mother turns a blind eye, exercising her own brand of cruelty. Families, Jaycee comes to believe, are “dangerous places … like nests of poisonous spiders, huddled in dark, undisturbed corners, their venom, a single drop enough to rot the body inside out”. Eventually taken into care, she finds an unlikely lifeline in Ella-G, another damaged girl whose exuberance masks wounds as profound as Jaycee’s own; both feel “on the outside of the world”. The care home turns out to be similarly brutal, and the pair survive together, forging a friendship that becomes the novel’s emotional anchor. Continue reading...
sources.title: Sky City by Jacqueline Crooks review – an ambitious, lyrical portrait of trauma

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The comedian and broadcaster narrates the heartfelt and at times self-lacerating account of his relationship with alcohol A memoir chronicling the comic and broadcaster John Robins’s life in alcohol and his subsequent path to sobriety, Thirst is structured around the drinks that changed his life. There’s the bottle of Jacob’s Creek wine left out on a kitchen worktop which he helped himself to at the age of seven, secreting it into his orange juice, and the beer given to him at scout camp which he drank alone. There’s also his stomach-churning recreation, while on a comedy tour of Australia, of the white russians drunk by the Dude in The Big Lebowski using a gallon of milk, a litre of vodka and a bottle of Kahlua. As an adult, Robins, who is best known for his shows on Radio X and on BBC5 Live, romanticised pubs, which he saw as places of peacefulness and refuge. He even co-hosted the podcast The Moon Under Water where he invited guests to describe their ideal pub. Robins reveals that what kept him drinking for so long was the lie that he was in control. That he could, on occasion, get through a Dry January convinced him he couldn’t be an addict, although he got a wakeup call when a GP told him to “sort your fucking life out”. Continue reading...
sources.title: Thirst by John Robins audiobook review – an ex-drinker’s darkly funny journey

thread_text:
新書《Sky City》，作者賈桂琳．克魯克斯（Jacqueline Crooks），描寫一名在1990年代倫敦公宅長大的女性潔西（Jaycee）。她童年遭繼父性侵，母親卻視而不見，後來被安置到寄養機構，與另一名同樣受創的女孩艾拉-G，建立起深厚的友誼。同一天，主持人約翰．羅賓斯（John Robins）推出有聲回憶錄《Thirst》，講述他從七歲偷喝酒，到後來走向戒酒的歷程。他形容自己曾把『還能控制』當成一種謊言——直到醫生勸他『把生活整頓好』，才真正意識到問題有多嚴重。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian 的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text: 有一本新書，寫的是一名童年受創的倫敦女性。書名《Sky City》，主角潔西，在1990年代的倫敦公宅長大，童年遭繼父性侵，母親卻視而不見，後來被安置到寄養機構，和另一名同樣受創的女孩，建立起深厚的友誼。同一天，主持人約翰．羅賓斯，推出了有聲回憶錄《Thirst》，講的是他從七歲偷喝酒，到後來走向戒酒的歷程。他說，自己曾把『還能控制』當成一種謊言，直到醫生勸他把生活整頓好，才真正意識到問題有多嚴重。
